chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Umrah, 'Is it obligatory?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said, 'So the one who performs Tamattu', would it suffice him from it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Performed Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: Is Umrah obligatory and does Tamattu' Hajj count as fulfilling it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) confirms that Umrah is an obligatory act (wajib), a ruling that distinguishes it from the Sunnah Umrah performed in conjunction with Hajj al-Qiran or Hajj al-Ifrad. The Imam further clarifies that the Umrah component of Hajj al-Tamattu' fully satisfies this obligation, highlighting the jurisprudential efficiency of the Tamattu' mode for pilgrims. This establishes a clear legal precedent in Shia fiqh regarding the sufficiency of Tamattu' Umrah for the primary duty of Umrah.

en.hubeali: A number of our companins, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said,
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about the Umra, ‘Is it Obligatory?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘So the one who performs Tumatto, would it suffice him from it?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al- £ Umrah; if it is obligatory. He (the Imam) said, £ Yes, it is obligatory.’ I then asked, ‘If one is for al-Tamattu £ (advantageous) is it sufficient?’ He (the Imam) said, £ Yes, it is sufficient.’” (Fatwa best explains Hadith 2 of this Chapter)
